Negative binomial regression by IRLS and Newton-Raphson

Source: R/nbreg.R
nbreg.Rd

Fits the NB2 regression model $$\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\theta$$ by maximum likelihood, alternating

  • IRLS for \(\beta\) with \(\theta\) fixed: working weights \(w_i = \theta\mu_i/(\theta+\mu_i)\), working response \(z_i = (\eta_i - o_i) + (y_i-\mu_i)/\mu_i\), \(\beta \leftarrow (X^\top WX)^{-1}X^\top Wz\); and

  • Newton-Raphson for \(\phi = \log\theta\) with \(\beta\) fixed,

Usage

nbreg(formula, data, offset, control = nbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A model formula, e.g. y ~ x1 + x2. Offsets may be given with offset() terms.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

Optional offset for the linear predictor (e.g. log exposure), evaluated in data.

control

A list from nbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "nbreg", a list with components coefficients, vcov, theta, SE.theta, loglik, iter, converged, fitted.values (\(\hat\mu\)), linear.predictors, residuals (response), y, offset, df.residual, nobs, trace (log-likelihood and \(\theta\) by iteration), call, terms, xlevels, contrasts and control.

Details

until the log-likelihood changes by less than control$tol. No general purpose optimizer is used. The parameterization is the one used by MASS::glm.nb().

Standard errors for \(\beta\) are from \((X^\top\hat WX)^{-1}\), treating \(\theta\) as known (as glm.nb() does), and \(\mathrm{SE}(\hat\theta) = \{-H(\hat\theta)\}^{-1/2}\).

See also

zinbreg(), nbreg-methods

Examples

# Simulated data with known beta = (1, 0.5) and theta = 2
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(300))
d$y <- rnbinom(300, size = 2, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -1.1750 -0.7653 -0.2194  0.3855  5.6578 
#> 
#> Coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  0.91318    0.05784  15.789  < 2e-16 ***
#> x            0.43526    0.05997   7.257 3.95e-13 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Theta = 1.78037 (SE 0.2737)
#> Log-likelihood: -626.523 on 3 Df,  AIC: 1259.046
#> Outer iterations (IRLS + Newton-Raphson): 3
#> 

# With an exposure offset
d$t <- runif(300, 1, 3)
d$y2 <- rnbinom(300, size = 2, mu = d$t * exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x))
coef(nbreg(y2 ~ x, data = d, offset = log(t)))
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   1.0929316   0.3934869
